title: The unchanged localization complex models and K-flat coefficient certificate
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site, R a sheaf of commutative rings and R_U its restriction to C/U. Use module sheaves and their standard unbounded derived category, with Q its complex localization and F_U the exact slice restriction. For a section f on U let S_f be the sheafification of V ↦ R_U(V)[1/f|V] [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Its degree-zero complex is K-flat. If P is bounded and each term is a finite coproduct of global section localizations, then F_U(P) is K-flat and Tot(S_f[0] tensor F_U(P)) is canonically isomorphic to the ordinary complex S_f tensor F_U(P). The coefficient tensor S_f tensor S_g is canonically isomorphic to S_(fg). The model definitions, exact restriction functors, standard derived functors and successive restriction comparison are exactly the unchanged constructions extracted from the parent module. Flatness and K-flatness use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat, lem-pc-sites-modules-sheafification-flat, lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site, lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat, lem-pc-sites-modules-coproduct-flat]; tensor products commute with sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor].

proof.text: Sectionwise localization is flat; evaluation jointly reflects limits, and sheafification of the flat presheaf is flat. The single complex in degree zero is bounded above and has flat terms, including its zero terms, hence is K-flat.

Retain the existing proofs: finite sums of localizations are flat, slice restriction preserves flatness and the upper bound, and the single-total tensor comparison identifies the ordinary tensor complex. Sectionwise localization tensor products identify with localization at the product and sheafify.
